essence: Sequence-bound entry into one's own nature announced.
The manifold-taught āṇava aims at Śiva-hood; penetration of its intervals, rest in the proximate station.
Ascent by abandonment: āṇava left for the Śākta plane, then the Śāmbhava — distinctly graded.
Crown: ray-flooded Bhairava-state, means-independence, eternal entry into the universe-wombed self.
Sealed as received teaching from the Supreme One.

rasa.dominant: śānta with adbhuta weight (rest as culmination; wonder at the ladder)
rasa.sthayibhava: śama (tranquillity) opening into camatkāra at the means-fall (v3)
rasa.justification: The ahnika rests — viśrāmyet (v1), nityam āviśati (v3) — and each rest deepens; wonder breaks through at the ray-flooded Bhairava expanse (v3) and the universe-wombed self, where attainment turns out to be homecoming.

sections.SUMMARY: Sequence-bound entry into one's own nature. The āṇava, manifoldly taught toward Śiva-hood, works through penetration of its own intervals and rest in the proximate station. Abandonment of the āṇava opens the Śākta plane; the same motion opens the Śāmbhava — each rung distinct in graded succession. The ladder's fruit: a Bhairava-state flooded with the rays of sequentially-dawned awakening, entered finally without means, forever, as one's own self holding the universe within. The teaching stands received from the Supreme One.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes the finale's ascent law: every means perfected by abandonment, the means-less entry as completion rather than refusal, recognition rather than acquisition as liberation's mechanism, and lineage authority as the seal of the whole thirty-seven-ahnika work.
sections.KEY TERMS: svasvarūpapraveśa (entry into one's own nature); krama (graded sequence binding the chapter); āṇava (lowest means: utterance, organ, meditation, phoneme, station); antar-antara (interval after interval, the āṇava's true field); savidha-pada (proximate-kindred station); saṃtyāga (abandonment as the engine of ascent); śāktī bhūmi and śāmbhavī (Śākta and Śāmbhava planes); tāratamya (more-and-less gradation); abhyupāya-nirapekṣatā (independence from means, the anupāya moment); garbhita-viśvarūpa (the universe-wombed self); parameṣṭhin (Supreme One: Śiva or supreme preceptor — LIVE).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Āhnika 34 closes the Tantraloka's doctrinal arc before the mantra compendium (ch30) and final rites: it returns to the upāya ladder of ch1 (śāmbhava/śākta/āṇava per Mālinīvijaya 2.21–23, quoted at TAL 1.168–170) and crowns it with the means-less entry of ch2 (anupāya, table-of-contents gatopāya; Tantrasara 1 caturvidham). Cross-links: a02 (anupāya doctrine), a01 (śāmbhava means and topics enunciation).
sections.EXPLANATION: The ahnika runs: (1) pratijñā — the sequence-bound entry announced; (2) the āṇava rung — manifold teaching, interval-penetration, proximate rest; (3) the ladder — abandon-and-resort repeated upward to Śākta then Śāmbhava, distinctly graded; (4) the crown — ray-flooded Bhairava-state, means-independence, eternal entry into the universe-wombed self; (5) the seal — told by the Supreme One, fork held open.
